metadata.title: CHSH Angle Explorer — The Formula the Dial Forgot
metadata.purpose: viz-riff critique: CHSH Angle Explorer — polar dial + four-correlation table + S gauge; polar geometry strong; CHSH formula never displayed; singlet subtitle stays wrong when state flips
metadata.reformat: center-cut, focus-aware; pantry/<bid>-916.* is the human replacement slot; -916 overrides honored

beats.narration_text: Ciao. Liam, in for Bear. Someone typed into Claude: build me a CHSH angle explorer — show why forty-five degrees beats the classical bound. Here is what came back. Today we judge the visualization. The Bell test physics gets a pass.

props.command: Hey Claude, write me a visualization for the CHSH inequality — show why 45° measurement spacing beats the classical bound.
output: ✓ S gauge — classical / quantum / Tsirelson zones

beats.narration_text: Two columns. Left: a polar dial labeled Measurement Angles. Four arrows from center — A-one and A-two in solid and dashed red; B-one and B-two in solid and dashed blue. Degree tick marks at forty-five-degree steps, labeled around the rim. Four preset buttons below: Optimal, All Same, Exercise-3, and the singlet state. Right: a large S display — currently 2.8284 — with text reading QUANTUM VIOLATION. Below it a two-by-two correlation table showing E of A-one B-one through E of A-two B-two. An S gauge with threshold lines. And four angle sliders.

A1 is Alice's first measurement angle. The capture sweeps it from zero to three-sixty while the other three angles hold at the optimal configuration. The A1 arrow sweeps the polar dial. Every correlation updates. S rises and falls. At zero degrees — optimal — S reaches 2.8284, two-root-two. Rotate A1 to ninety, same as A2, and S collapses near zero. The S box switches between red-bordered QUANTUM VIOLATION and plain LOCAL REALIST REGIME each time S crosses the classical threshold of two.

Three things right. One: the polar dial makes the forty-five-degree argument visual. At optimal, four arrows partition the circle symmetrically — the geometry IS the claim. No algebra required. Two: the S gauge encodes three regimes in one bar — white inside the classical bound, red shading in the quantum region, blue dashes at the Tsirelson limit. You read which side of history S is on before you read the number. Three: the S box label changes state — QUANTUM VIOLATION, CLASSICAL BOUNDARY, LOCAL REALIST REGIME — only when the physics warrants it. The classification is tied to the value, not the aesthetics.

Let's recap with Claude. Polar dial makes the forty-five-degree geometry visual — the argument lives in the arrow layout. Three color zones on the S gauge place S in its regime before the number is read. Singlet preset flips E values correctly but leaves the triplet equation in the subtitle — the formula is now wrong on screen. The CHSH formula with its asymmetric minus sign on E of A-two B-two is never displayed. Best used after students know the inequality. The one fix: add that formula between the correlation table and the S box.

artifactLines: Polar dial makes 45° geometry visual — argument is in the arrow layout
S gauge encodes three regimes — classical / quantum / Tsirelson in one bar
Singlet preset flips correlations correctly but leaves triplet equation in subtitle
CHSH formula S = E₁₁ + E₁₂ + E₂₁ − E₂₂ never displayed — minus sign invisible
